summary: order-service p99 >5s and ~9% 5xx errors beginning ~09:00Z are a downstream symptom. Root cause is deployment dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0, 08:56Z) which added an unindexed holdings P&L query on the 48M-row `trades` table, forcing a Seq Scan per request. Because ledger-db is a shared datastore, the resulting CPU saturation (~96%) and connection explosion (62->190) blocked order-service INSERT INTO orders, which the DB then cancelled via statement timeout from 09:00:42Z. order-service was not released this week. The DBA's autovacuum config change (cfg-2903, 08:00Z) is a red herring: it applied 58 min before onset, only touched public.audit_log, and ledger-db had no anomaly between 07:00 and 08:58Z.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unindexed portfolio-service P&L query (dep-5905) saturates shared ledger-db, timing out order-service INSERTs
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0, 08:56Z) added a holdings P&L query on the large `trades` table filtered by account_id + executed_at with no supporting index and no migration. This forces a Seq Scan on 48M rows per request, driving ledger-db CPU to ~96% and slow queries to ~140/min. Since ledger-db is a shared datastore, order-service INSERT INTO orders statements can no longer complete and are cancelled by the DB statement timeout, producing the order-service p99 > 5s and ~9% 5xx errors. order-service itself was not changed.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 deploys v4.5.0 adding an unindexed query on trades (no migration/index)
First ledger-db slow queries appear 08:58:38Z, all from portfolio-service doing a Seq Scan on trades (48M rows)
order-service INSERT INTO orders blocks on the saturated shared DB and is cancelled by statement timeout from 09:00:42Z
order-service error_rate jumps to 8.94% at 09:00Z and p99 to ~5.3s

assumptions: The `trades` table lacks an index on (account_id, executed_at) so the new query degrades to a seq scan (log shows 'Seq Scan on trades')
The statement timeouts in order-service are caused by DB CPU/queue contention, not a separate fault

ranked_hypotheses.title: Autovacuum tuning change (cfg-2903) on ledger-db caused the degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The DBA's cfg-2903 change (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1) at 08:00Z made autovacuum more aggressive, causing extra I/O/CPU on ledger-db and slowing queries including order-service inserts.
assumptions: More aggressive autovacuum could raise DB CPU enough to time out unrelated writes
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing mismatch: cfg-2903 applied at 08:00:20Z but onset is 08:51-08:58Z (58 min later) and ledger-db logs show no anomaly between 07:00 and 08:58Z (F13). The slow queries are all the portfolio-service seq scan (F4), not autovacuum, and autovacuum only touched public.audit_log (F11).

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db infrastructure/IOPS or resource failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The ledger-db storage/IO subsystem failed or throttled, causing slow queries and statement timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: No infra error logs and specific new query pattern

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The slow queries are explicitly attributed to a specific new portfolio-service seq-scan query (F4); no storage/IO error logs and no rollback/failover evidence. Mirrors HIST-111 (bad_deployment).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Traffic surge / capacity saturation on ledger-db
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A load increase outgrew ledger-db provisioned capacity, saturating CPU and timing out order-service writes.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: order-service and portfolio-service request rates are flat across the onset (F12); the added DB load comes from a new unindexed query, not more traffic.

facts.statement: order-service p99 went from ~150ms to ~5.3s with onset in the 08:51 bucket.
order-service error_rate jumped from 0.22% at 08:59 to 8.94% at 09:00 (per-minute).
order-service errors are exclusively ledger-db statement timeouts on INSERT INTO orders, first seen 09:00:42Z.
ledger-db slow queries are all portfolio-service 'SELECT * FROM trades ... Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)', first seen 08:58:38Z.
ledger-db CPU rose to ~96%, slow_queries to ~140/min, connections to ~190 after the onset.
dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0) deployed 08:56Z added a new query on trades filtered by account_id+executed_at with no migration/index, and is live.
The only config change, cfg-2903 autovacuum tuning, applied at 08:00:20Z and only autovacuumed public.audit_log.
Request rates were flat for order-service (~230 req/s) and portfolio-service (~570 req/s) across the onset.
ledger-db had no WARN/ERROR logs between 07:00 and 08:58Z; the pattern began at 08:58:38Z.
ledger-db is a shared postgres datastore used by both order-service and portfolio-service.

assumptions: The `trades` table lacks an index on (account_id, executed_at), so the new query degrades to a seq scan (explicitly shown as 'Seq Scan on trades' in logs).
order-service statement timeouts are caused by ledger-db CPU/queue contention, not a separate order-service fault.
Deployment timestamps correspond to actual traffic effect within the minute-level recording resolution.

timeline.event: DBA config change cfg-2903 (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2->0.1) applied on ledger-db
Deployment dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0) rollout complete, adding unindexed trades query
First ledger-db slow query: portfolio-service seq scan on trades (48M rows)
First order-service 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' error
Incident reported; ledger-db CPU ~96%, slow queries ~140/min, order p99 ~5.4s

recommended_actions.action: Roll back / revert portfolio-service deployment dep-5905 (v4.5.0) immediately to remove the unindexed trades query.
recommended_actions.rationale: The new seq-scan query is the source of ledger-db saturation; removing it should restore order-service within minutes.

recommended_actions.action: Add a composite index on trades(account_id, executed_at) (CONCURRENTLY) and re-deploy the P&L feature behind a query-review gate.
recommended_actions.rationale: Eliminates the seq scan so the feature can be re-enabled safely; matches HIST-111 resolution.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on ledger-db CPU, slow_queries_per_min and connections_active, and per-application slow-query attribution, so a single tenant's query can be caught before it saturates the shared DB.
recommended_actions.rationale: The DB saturated silently for ~2 minutes before order-service errors surfaced.

recommended_actions.action: Add a deployment-time guard that flags queries touching large tables without a supporting index.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of unindexed seq-scan queries on shared datastores (same class as HIST-111).

data_gaps: No direct EXPLAIN/index listing for the `trades` table was available; the missing index is inferred from the 'Seq Scan on trades' log annotation rather than confirmed catalog state.
order-service logs were truncated (returned 30 of 70 matches) and ledger-db slow-query logs truncated (30 of 94); pattern and first-seen are consistent but full enumeration not retrieved.
No rollback of dep-5905 has occurred, so recovery-after-revert could not be directly observed to fully close the causal loop.
